Courchevel turns 80 this winter. The resort, built from scratch in 1946, opens its season on 4 December 2026, and its grandest houses open with it. The season runs until 18 April 2027, and the first day starts with a free breakfast on the Courchevel 1850 snow front.

## The palaces return

Cheval Blanc Courchevel, the LVMH maison, and Airelles Courchevel both reopen on 4 December. Cheval Blanc adds two private chalets opposite the Maison this winter. Fouquet's Courchevel, the Barrière palace, opens from 5 December according to the resort's listing, with Loulou, its Parisian trattoria, at the heart of the après-ski. Aman Le Mélézin follows on 10 December, and Maisons Pariente's Hôtel Saint Roch, now 37 keys, on 18 December.

## New names in 1850

Bourbon Hotel, 31 rooms in place of the former Hôtel des 3 Vallées, now belongs to Chapitre Six, with Simonetta, an Italian table by chef Simone Zanoni. At K2 Altitude, L'Altitude has won its first MICHELIN star under Guillaume Duchemin and Davide Sessa. The resort counts seven starred restaurants and eleven stars in total. Last winter brought 1.19 million skier-days.

## The signal

At 80, Courchevel keeps adding great addresses, and the 2030 Olympic speed races will finish on L'Éclipse. Alpine resorts now compete on the depth of their hotel line-up as much as on their snow.

Happy 80th winter to Courchevel and to all its hotel teams.
summary: The resort turns 80 and opens on 4 December, with Cheval Blanc, Airelles and Fouquet's Courchevel back for the season.
title: Courchevel turns 80: Cheval Blanc, Airelles and Fouquet's reopen
why: The Alps' most glamorous resort celebrates 80 years with its palaces.
